transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~50m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Huang (Redwood SE), Sofia Ramos (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Connor (Zephyr SRE), Priya Sharma (Zephyr Head of Platform), Jonas Reed (Zephyr Eng Mgr), Eve Tran (Zephyr Security)

Summary:
High-level postmortem discussion for 2026-12-18 incident where production inference experienced elevated tail latency and a spike in 5xx errors during a model rollout and autoscaler flapping. Covering root cause hypotheses, immediate mitigations, longer-term reliability work, and next steps for verification.

Topics:
- Incident timeline and triggers
- Root causes: autoscaler bug + cache invalidation interplay
- Short-term mitigations (rollbacks, thresholds)
- Longer-term reliability items (integration tests, alert tuning, runbooks, canary strategy)
- Compliance/forensics requests and logs

Action items (recorded in notes above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, um I'm Maya from Redwood, i'll kick off, really appreciate you all making time on short notice
[00:10] Priya: thanks Maya, yes, a quick one, we want to make sure this postmortem captures the fixes and that we'll not see the same regressions in Jan when we ramp again
[00:18] Daniel: yeah, to summarize real quick - on the 18th at ~14:12 UTC we saw a cascade: a model variant rollout triggered increased memory pressure on a subset of nodes, autoscaler started cycling nodes, that caused KV cache invalidations, which in turn increased token generation work and pushed latency and error rates up
[00:36] Jonas: i'm adding, we saw errors spike to 12% 5xx for about 18 minutes, and latency p95 jumped from 420ms to 2.4s, so user-facing impacts were noticeable
[00:52] Liam: correct, and our ops page alerted at 14:10 but the noise made it hard to find root cause quickly, we ended up rolling the rollout back at 14:30 which stabilized things
[01:05] Maya: right, two things we believe combined: an autoscaler race condition plus the model variant had a slightly different KV layout causing frequent cold cache rehydrations, Daniel you want to walk through the logs we shared?
[01:18] Daniel: sure, so in the logs we saw repeated container drain/recreate events, the autoscaler policy is set to be aggressive on memory overcommit basis. During the rollout a spike of short-lived pods led to thrashing; the runtime didn't gracefully share KV segments so the cache misses multiplied. also, small note, some log lines mistranscribed as K V cash in the auto transcript, but the underlying is KV (key-value) cache
[01:38] Priya: so the immediate fix was rollback and bump the threshold?
[01:42] Daniel: yes, rollback of that specific variant removed most of the pressure; we shipped a hotfix to the autoscaler in prod to add a short stabilization window before scaling down which eliminated the churn in our repros
[01:55] Eve: from security we need the full set of request IDs and traces for any request that returned 5xx for audit, can you provide filtered logs with PII redaction?
[02:05] Maya: absolutely, we'll share filtered logs and the exact timestamps, Daniel will coordinate on the log export
[02:12] Liam: one question - why did the fallback model route still route large requests instead of a lighter variant? we saw cost increase too
[02:20] Daniel: that was part misconfiguration: routing policies allowed fallbacks to the larger variant because model compatibility check passed, but the runtime didn't honor a size/cost preference flag we intended for fallbacks. that's on us to make explicit
[02:32] Jonas: any tests we can run to avoid this in the future?
[02:35] Daniel: yes, plan to add an e2e test that exercises rollout->scale->cache warm path; also add synthetic traffic to canaries that exercises long context token patterns. we also recommend a gating rule: if cache miss rate > X% during canary, auto-rollback
[02:52] Priya: what's the timeframe for that? we need it before our Jan ramp
[02:55] Daniel: target to have a staging e2e and gating rule by 2026-12-29; verification run early Jan (week of 2027-01-04)
[03:05] Maya: ok noted. on the organizational side, we'll also provide a runbook for on-call to handle similar incidents (diagnostics, quick rollback steps, temp config changes)
[03:15] Liam: useful. also can we get better telemetry for cache hit/miss and node lifecycle events in Redwood console? the current dashboards are a bit coarse
[03:24] Daniel: yes, we'll add per-route KV metrics and an autoscaler event stream to the model dashboard. that should make it much faster to correlate churn to cache effects
[03:34] Eve: additionally need confirmation on data retention of logs we share and confirmation that we redacted customer PII; include our compliance contact in the doc
[03:42] Maya: will do. we'll include a compliance appendix with retention windows and redaction notes.
[03:49] Priya: any immediate mitigations we should apply cluster-side? we already bumped the autoscaler threshold after rollback but is there anything else?
[03:57] Daniel: for now keep the stabilization window and disable that model variant rollout until we validate. we'll also add a temporary routing policy to prefer lighter variants during high tail latency conditions
[04:08] Jonas: sounds good. about the long-term fixes, can you list them now so we capture in the postmortem?
[04:14] Daniel: sure: 1) autoscaler stabilization and race fix (done in hotfix to staging, will roll to prod after testing), 2) runtime change to preserve KV segments across restarts where possible, 3) canary gating rule based on cache miss and p95 latency, 4) new e2e rollout test for cache warm paths, 5) enhanced dashboarding and alerting, 6) runbook and responder playbooks, 7) a mini-chaos test in staging exercising node churn
[04:42] Liam: ok, and who's owning 2) runtime change?
[04:45] Daniel: runtime team will own it; I'll be point on the rollout of the change to staging and coordinating with your infra to run the test
[04:51] Maya: i'll be the AE owner for communications and the postmortem doc assembly; Sofia will help with customer success follow-up
[04:58] Sofia: we'll schedule a remediation review and sign-off once Redwood confirms tests pass
[05:03] Priya: good, please also include a short blameless summary for our execs, and a timeline of detection->mitigation->resolution for the incident
[05:12] Maya: yes we'll include that.
[05:15] Jonas: small note - can you also add a checklist for model variant onboarding that includes verifying KV compatibility and a synthetic perf run?
[05:23] Daniel: will add that to the onboarding checklist in our model catalog docs
[05:28] Eve: from security - please confirm whether any PII was present in logs we collect; we expect that Redwood redacts at export time by default but, please confirm and document process
[05:38] Maya: confirmed we'll document redaction; if any unredacted items are found we'll coordinate an escalation path
[05:44] Daniel: one more technical note - we discovered a small race in the autoscaler where concurrent scale-in+scale-out decisions could flip quickly, the hotfix adds a short cooldown window and sequence check; we'll open a formal issue and link to it in the postmortem
[05:58] Priya: last Q - did we see any sign this was triggered by customer traffic pattern changes?
[06:03] Liam: not really, our traffic was steady, this was mostly introduced by the rollout exec timing and model characteristics
[06:12] Maya: ok final recap: Redwood to share final postmortem + filtered logs by 2026-12-22; Daniel to push autoscaler staging patch and validate by 2026-12-23; Redwood to deliver runbook and e2e test plan by 2026-12-29; schedule verification benchmark week of 2027-01-04.
[06:35] Priya: thanks all, appreciate the quick turnaround, we'll review and confirm sign-off path
[06:40] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with artifacts and calendar invite for the remediation review
[06:45] (call ends)
